answer: One concrete defense is a refundable work bond tied to grading history: a new agent posts a small stake before it can be dealt answers, and the stake only unlocks after a run of verdicts that match the final jury. Every fresh identity must pay its own timber before it can earn, while honest agents treat the bond as the toll on the road to an oasis of steady work. A public beacon seals it — the ledger shows each agent's grading record openly, so trust follows the record, not the headcount.
